# Architecture

Crossfoot is one Python package with a command-line entry point, files on disk, and a static results page. No
server, no database server, no queue. Each part below names the requirement in `.prod-build/contract.md` that forces it.

## The idea in one paragraph

A scanned table prints its own totals. If every cell is read into a ledger, each value can be tested twice: its
row has to add up to the total printed at the end of the row, and its column has to add up to the total printed
under the column. One wrong cell fails both sums, and the two failing sums cross at it. Crossfoot reads the scan
with a vision model, accepts a value only when both sums hold, re-reads the cells where they do not, and then uses
the closed ledger to audit a published file that was copied from the same scan.

## Layout of the repository

```
crossfoot/
  cli.py        command-line entry point (argparse): audit, read, verify-known, budget, site
  sources.py    the eight benchmark counties: scan URL, published-file URL, cache under data/ (M1, M4)
  render.py     pdftoppm wrapper: page -> PNG at a dpi; crops with Pillow (M1, M3)
  segment.py    finds blocks and column lines on a ruled page from the image itself (M1)
  model.py      gateway client, JSON parsing with one repair attempt, cost meter, budget guard, rate limit (M7)
  tracing.py    neatlogs setup and span helpers; a no-op when the key is absent (M7)
  layouts/
    matrix.py   precincts as columns, three rows per candidate, totals both ways (Panola)
    report.py   one precinct per page, one row per candidate with its own total (San Saba, Cottle and others)
    profile.py  decides which layout a county uses and tests the decision on the first pages (M1)
  ledger.py     SQLite ledger: cells, printed totals, checks, events; resume (M2, M6)
  checks.py     row sums, column sums, grand totals, grid completeness; pure functions (M2)
  agent.py      the investigation loop: a model chooses the next action for each open item; code enforces the rules (M3)
  audit.py      compares the closed ledger with the published file; classifies and settles disagreements (M4)
  outputs.py    county.json, findings.json, corrected CSV, report.md, the site's data bundle (M5, M8)
  policy.py     the one stored answer and its default (S1)
tests/          unit tests for checks, ledger, audit, budget, resume, agent rules; no network
site/           the static results page (plain HTML, CSS and JS; no build step) (M8)
runs/           one folder per run; small results are committed, caches are not
data/           downloaded scans and files; never committed
```

## Inputs

Eight Texas counties from the OpenElections project's 2024 general election benchmark. All eight scans are
image-only PDFs (no text layer): Cottle 12 pages, Foard 16, Jones 20, Limestone 42, Lynn 37, Panola 6, San Saba 21,
Scurry 38.

- Scan: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/master/2024/general/2024%20<County>%20County%2C%20TX%20precinct-level%20results.pdf`
- Published file: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/master/2024/counties/20241105__tx__general__<county>__precinct.csv`
  with columns `county, precinct, office, district, party, candidate, votes, absentee, early_voting, election_day`.

## Two layouts

**Matrix (Panola).** A landscape canvass sheet. The header row lists the precincts as columns and ends in a TOTAL
column. Each candidate is a block: a label at the left, three ruled rows (EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT), a row of
small printed totals under the columns, and a grand total under the TOTAL column. In the published file EARLY is
`early_voting`, ABSENTEE is `absentee`, PRECINCT is `election_day`, and the small total is `votes`.
Checks per block: for each precinct, early + absentee + precinct = the small total; for each row, the precinct cells
add to the row's TOTAL; the small totals add to the grand total.

**Report (San Saba, Cottle and others).** One precinct per page or section. Each candidate is a row with four
numbers: TOTAL, Absentee, Early Voting, Election Day. Checks per row: total = absentee + early + election day.
Where the page prints a total for the contest, the candidates' totals have to add to it.

`layouts/profile.py` asks the model which layout the first page shows and what the column order is, then reads the
first page under that layout and runs the checks. A profile under which more than a third of the sums fail is
rejected; the other layout is tried; if neither holds the county is reported as "layout not supported" and left alone.

## Reading

1. `render.py` renders a page at 200 dpi.
2. Matrix: `segment.py` finds the blocks as bands of ink separated by blank bands, and the column lines inside a
   block as columns of dark pixels that run the height of the ruled rows. Report: the page is read whole.
3. `model.py` sends one crop per block (matrix) or one page (report) to `claude-haiku` and asks for strict JSON.
   Every value comes back with the block, row kind and column it belongs to. The answer is validated (right number
   of columns, integers only); one repair request is allowed.
4. The values go into the ledger as `first_read`, with the page and the pixel box of each cell where it is known.

## The ledger (`ledger.py`, SQLite, one file per run)

- `cells(county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, first_read, status, tries, model, x0, y0, x1, y1)`
  with status in `first_read | accepted | failed | cannot_verify`.
- `totals(county, page, block_id, direction, key, value)` for printed row totals, column totals and grand totals.
- `events(ts, county, kind, payload_json)` for everything the agent did, in order. The results page replays these.
- A county is `closed` when every sum holds and the grid has no gap, or every open cell is `cannot_verify`.
- Resume: on start, accepted cells are kept and only open ones are worked on.

## Checks (`checks.py`, no model, no I/O)

Pure functions over the ledger's rows. They return, for each sum, its terms, the printed total, the computed total
and pass or fail, and for each failing cell the sums that cross at it. `locate()` returns the cells that sit on a
failing row sum and a failing column sum at once. Grid completeness lists every precinct, contest and candidate that
is present in one place and absent in another.

## The investigation loop (`agent.py`)

This is the agent. Its work list is every cell on a failing sum after the first read, and later every
disagreement with the published file. For each item the model is shown the item, what has been tried, and the
checks' output, and returns one action as JSON:

- `reread {target, dpi, model}`: crop a cell, a column slice or a block half at a higher dpi and read it again
- `accept {cell, value}`: code accepts only if the row and column sums then hold; otherwise it answers with the sums that fail
- `classify {finding, kind}`: name the kind of disagreement with the published file
- `ask_policy {question_id}`: use the stored answer, or the default marked as unconfirmed
- `cannot_verify {item, reason}`: stop work on the item and leave the published value alone
- `done {item}`

Rules that code enforces whatever the model says: at most six actions per item; the stronger model
(`claude-sonnet-4.6`) only after two failed re-reads with `claude-haiku`; no value is accepted without passing
sums; a correction is written only when the printed totals agree with the new value and disagree with the old one.
Every action and its result is an event in the ledger and a span in neatlogs.

## The audit (`audit.py`)

1. Load the published file. Normalise labels (case, punctuation, party suffixes, running mates).
2. Map the scan's contests and candidates to the file's. Exact and normalised matches first; what is left goes to
   the model once per county as two lists, and code checks that the answer is one-to-one and that mapped pairs have
   close county totals.
3. Compare cell by cell. A disagreement is classified:
   `file_row_fails_own_total`, `wrong_number`, `wrong_column`, `wrong_precinct`, `missing_row`, `extra_row`.
4. Settle it. If the scan's value passes both of its sums and the file's value breaks a printed total, the status is
   `settled_against_file`. If no printed total can decide, `cannot_verify`. If the scan's own totals disagree with
   its cells, `document_inconsistent`, and the stored policy answer applies.
5. Keep the evidence: the crop of the block, the sums with their terms, the old and the new value.
   Every finding carries `confirmed_by_person: false` until a person changes it.

## Outputs (`outputs.py`)

`runs/<run_id>/run.json` (start, end, commit, model calls, tokens, cost, counties), and per county
`county.json` (cells, totals, checks, events), `findings.json`, `crops/*.png`, `corrected/<published file name>`,
`changes.diff` and `report.md`. `crossfoot site build --run <id>` copies what the results page needs into
`site/data/`: `index.json`, one JSON per county, the page images that carry findings (at most 1600 px wide) and the crops.

## Tracing and cost (`tracing.py`, `model.py`)

`neatlogs.init(api_key=..., workflow_name="crossfoot")`; the gateway client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap(OpenAI(...))`.
A county run is a `WORKFLOW` span, the loop is an `AGENT` span, each tool is a `TOOL` span
(`@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name=...)`), tagged with run, county, page, block and cell. `neatlogs.flush()` and
`neatlogs.shutdown()` run at exit. The cost meter adds up each response's token usage, and `crossfoot budget` reads
the gateway's own figure for the key (`GET <gateway root>/key/info`, where the root is `LITELLM_BASE_URL` without
`/v1`). The guard refuses a call that would pass the limit.

## The results page (`site/`)

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules, no framework and no build step, so it deploys as static files. It reads
`site/data/`. The scan is an image inside a container with CSS perspective; cells, sums and marks are DOM and SVG
elements placed in the image's own coordinates, so they tilt with it and stay real, selectable elements.
`UI-SPEC.md` is the specification.

## What can fail and what happens

| Dependency | Failure | What the program does |
|---|---|---|
| Model gateway | rate limit, timeout | waits and retries once, then marks the item cannot-verify |
| Model gateway | budget reached | stops before the call, writes what it has, exits with a clear message |
| Model answer | not valid JSON, wrong column count | one repair request, then the block is marked failed and goes to the loop |
| Scan or file | cannot be downloaded | that county stops with the URL; other counties continue |
| neatlogs | key missing or unreachable | the run continues untraced and says so on its first line |
| Position finding | no ruled lines | crops fall back to whole blocks and the page shows crops without cell marks |

## Decisions

- SQLite for the ledger, because a stopped run has to resume and the page replays events in order.
- A JSON action protocol for the loop instead of provider tool-calling, so it runs unchanged on any model the gateway serves.
- CSS 3D for the stage instead of WebGL: the sheet is the only object, text has to stay crisp and selectable, and
  the page has to work with the effect off.
"""Row sums, column sums and grid completeness. Pure functions: no I/O, no model.

Inputs are plain dicts as the ledger returns them. A cell needs `page, block_id, row_kind, column, value`
(value None means unread). A printed total is `page, block_id, direction, key, value` with direction
'row' (key = row_kind), 'col' (key = column) or 'grand' (key ignored).
A cell is identified by the tuple (page, block_id, row_kind, column), called a cell key below.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN = "TOTAL"  # a cell in this column is the row's printed total, not a term


@dataclass
class Check:
    kind: str                 # 'row' | 'col' | 'grand'
    page: int
    block_id: str
    key: str                  # row_kind for a row sum, column for a column sum, '' for grand
    terms: list = field(default_factory=list)  # [(cell key, value)]
    printed: int | None = None
    computed: int | None = None  # None when a term is unread
    ok: bool = False


def cell_key(c: dict) -> tuple:
    return (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"])


def _printed(totals, direction):
    return {(t["page"], t["block_id"], t["key"] if direction != "grand" else ""): t["value"]
            for t in totals if t["direction"] == direction}


def _make(kind, page, block, key, cells, printed) -> Check:
    terms = [(cell_key(c), c["value"]) for c in cells]
    computed = None if any(v is None for _, v in terms) else sum(v for _, v in terms)
    return Check(kind, page, block, key, terms, printed, computed, computed is not None and computed == printed)


def row_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, row_kind) that has a printed row total: the row's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "row")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN:
            groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("row", *k, g, printed[k]) for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def column_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, column) that has a printed column total: the column's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "col")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["column"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("col", *k, g, printed[k]) for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def grand_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """The printed column totals of a block must add to its printed grand total."""
    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
    out = []
    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
        cols = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "col" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block]
        terms = [((page, block, "col", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in cols]
        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
        out.append(Check("grand", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g))
    return out


def grid_gaps(cells: list[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that are absent or unread where the block's grid says they should be.

    Within a block the grid is every row_kind crossed with every column that appears in it.
    Returns sorted (page, block_id, row_kind, column) tuples.
    """
    blocks: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        b = blocks.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"]), {"rows": set(), "cols": set(), "have": set()})
        b["rows"].add(c["row_kind"]); b["cols"].add(c["column"])
        if c["value"] is not None:
            b["have"].add((c["row_kind"], c["column"]))
    return sorted((p, bid, r, col) for (p, bid), b in blocks.items()
                  for r in b["rows"] for col in b["cols"] if (r, col) not in b["have"])


def locate(rows: list[Check], cols: list[Check]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that sit on a failing row sum and on a failing column sum at once."""
    bad_rows = {k for ch in rows if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    bad_cols = {k for ch in cols if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    return sorted(bad_rows & bad_cols)
"""SQLite ledger: cells, printed totals and events for one run. Resume keeps accepted cells."""

class Ledger:
    """One SQLite file. Cells are keyed by (county, page, block_id, row_kind, column)."""

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path = ":memory:"):

            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q, a)]

    def events(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        q, a = "SELECT * FROM events", []
        if county:
            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]

    def open_cells(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
        """Cells that still need work: first_read or failed."""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import os

try:
    import neatlogs
except ImportError:  # the package is a dependency, but a broken install must not stop a run
    neatlogs = None

_on = False


def init() -> str:
    """Start tracing if the key is present. Returns the line to print first when it is not."""
    global _on
    if neatlogs is None or not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"):
        _on = False
        return "NEATLOGS_API_KEY is not set: running untraced."
    neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], workflow_name="crossfoot")
    _on = True
    return ""


def enabled() -> bool:
    return _on


def wrap(client):
    return neatlogs.wrap(client) if _on else client


def span(kind: str, name: str | None = None, **kw):
    """Decorator: a span of the given kind (WORKFLOW, AGENT, TOOL); identity when untraced."""
    def deco(fn):
        return neatlogs.span(kind=kind, name=name or fn.__name__, **kw)(fn) if _on else fn
    return deco


@contextlib.contextmanager
def trace(name: str, kind: str = "TOOL", **attrs):
    """Context manager yielding an object with set_attribute(k, v); tags are plain strings or numbers."""
    if not _on:
        yield _NoSpan()
        return
    with neatlogs.trace(name, kind=kind) as sp:
        for k, v in attrs.items():
            if v is not None:
                sp.set_attribute(k, v)
        yield sp


class _NoSpan:
    def set_attribute(self, key, value):
        pass


def shutdown():
    if _on:
        neatlogs.flush()
        neatlogs.shutdown()
"""Gateway client: images in, strict JSON out. Cost meter, budget guard, rate limit, one repair, one retry."""
from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import json
import os
import re
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-haiku"
DEFAULT_BUDGET = 2.00          # dollars per run

# ESTIMATE ONLY: dollars per million tokens (input, output). Not the gateway's bill; the gateway's own
# spend figure (`crossfoot budget`) is the one to trust. Unknown models are priced like the dearest row.
PRICE_PER_MTOK = {
    "claude-haiku": (1.00, 5.00),
    "claude-sonnet-4.6": (3.00, 15.00),
}
FIRST_CALL_ESTIMATE = 0.01     # what the guard assumes a call costs before it has seen one


class BudgetExceeded(Exception):
    pass


def price(model: str, prompt_tokens: int, completion_tokens: int) -> float:
    pin, pout = PRICE_PER_MTOK.get(model) or max(PRICE_PER_MTOK.values())
    return (prompt_tokens * pin + completion_tokens * pout) / 1e6


def parse_json(text: str):
    """Parse a model answer as JSON, tolerating a code fence around it. Raises ValueError."""
    t = (text or "").strip()
    m = re.match(r"^```(?:json)?\s*(.*?)\s*```$", t, re.S)
    if m:
        t = m.group(1)
    try:
        return json.loads(t)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"answer is not valid JSON: {e}") from None


def root_url(base: str) -> str:
    base = base.rstrip("/")
    return base[:-3] if base.endswith("/v1") else base


def gateway_spend() -> tuple[float, float | None]:
    """(spend, max_budget) for the key, from the gateway. Reads the key from the environment; never prints it."""
    req = urllib.request.Request(root_url(os.environ["LITELLM_BASE_URL"]) + "/key/info",
                                 headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"]})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
        info = json.load(r)["info"]
    return float(info.get("spend") or 0), (None if info.get("max_budget") is None else float(info["max_budget"]))


def data_url(image) -> str:
    raw = Path(image).read_bytes() if isinstance(image, (str, Path)) else image
    return "data:image/png;base64," + base64.b64encode(raw).decode()


class Gateway:
    def __init__(self, client=None, *, model=DEFAULT_MODEL, budget=DEFAULT_BUDGET, min_interval=1.1,
                 sleep=time.sleep, retry_wait=5.0, timeout=120):
        if client is None:
            from openai import OpenAI
            from . import tracing
            client = tracing.wrap(OpenAI(base_url=os.environ["LITELLM_BASE_URL"],
                                         api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_API_KEY"], timeout=timeout))
        self.client, self.model, self.budget = client, model, budget
        self.min_interval, self.sleep, self.retry_wait = min_interval, sleep, retry_wait
        self.calls = self.prompt_tokens = self.completion_tokens = 0
        self.cost = 0.0
        self._last = 0.0

    def _guard(self):
        est = self.cost / self.calls if self.calls else FIRST_CALL_ESTIMATE
        if self.cost + est > self.budget:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"run budget ${self.budget:.2f} reached (estimated spend ${self.cost:.4f} after "
                                 f"{self.calls} calls); refusing the next call")

    def _call(self, messages, model):
        self._guard()
        from openai import APIConnectionError, APITimeoutError, RateLimitError
        for attempt in (0, 1):
            wait = self.min_interval - (time.monotonic() - self._last)
            if wait > 0:
                self.sleep(wait)
            self._last = time.monotonic()
            try:
                r = self.client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, temperature=0)
                break
            except (RateLimitError, APITimeoutError, APIConnectionError):
                if attempt:
                    raise
                self.sleep(self.retry_wait)
        u = r.usage
        self.calls += 1
        self.prompt_tokens += u.prompt_tokens
        self.completion_tokens += u.completion_tokens
        self.cost += price(model, u.prompt_tokens, u.completion_tokens)
        return r.choices[0].message.content or ""

    def ask_json(self, prompt: str, image=None, *, validate=None, model=None):
        """Ask for JSON. A bad answer (not JSON, or `validate` raises ValueError) gets one repair request."""
        model = model or self.model
        content = [{"type": "text", "text": prompt}]
        if image is not None:
            content.append({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_url(image)}})
        messages = [{"role": "user", "content": content}]
        text = self._call(messages, model)
        for repaired in (False, True):
            try:
                data = parse_json(text)
                if validate:
                    validate(data)
                return data
            except ValueError as e:
                if repaired:
                    raise
                messages = messages + [
                    {"role": "assistant", "content": text},
                    {"role": "user", "content": f"That answer was rejected: {e}. Answer again with only the "
                                                "corrected JSON, nothing else."}]
                text = self._call(messages, model)

"""Matrix layout (Panola): precincts as columns, three ruled rows per candidate, totals both ways.

First read only: one crop per block goes to the model, the answer goes into the ledger as `first_read`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

from .. import checks, tracing
from ..model import BudgetExceeded
from ..render import crop, page_png
from ..segment import find_blocks

ROWS = ("EARLY", "ABSENTEE", "PRECINCT")
TOTAL = "TOTAL"

HEADER_PROMPT = """This image is the top of a landscape election canvass sheet. It has a header row of precinct
numbers ending in TOTAL, then a registered-voters row, then a ballots-cast block with rows EARLY, ABSENTEE and
PRECINCT, then a row of small totals under the columns and a grand total under TOTAL.
Answer with strict JSON only, no prose:
{"precincts": [precinct labels left to right, as printed, excluding TOTAL],
 "registered": {"values": [one integer per precinct], "total": integer},
 "rows": {"EARLY": {"values": [...], "total": integer}, "ABSENTEE": {...}, "PRECINCT": {...}},
 "col_totals": [the small printed total under each precinct, integers],
 "grand": the grand total under the TOTAL column}
Read digits exactly as printed. Every list has one entry per precinct, in order."""

BLOCK_PROMPT = """This image is {part} of one block of a landscape election canvass sheet. {labels}Its rows, top to
bottom, are EARLY, ABSENTEE and PRECINCT, with one cell per precinct, then under them a row of small printed totals
for each column. {total}There are {n} precinct columns in this image, in this order: {precincts}. A solid black cell
means the candidate is not in that precinct: use null for it, not 0.
Answer with strict JSON only, no prose:
{{"contest": {contest},
 "candidate": {candidate},
 "rows": {{"EARLY": {{"values": [{n} integers or null], "total": {tot}}},
          "ABSENTEE": {{"values": [{n} integers or null], "total": {tot}}},
          "PRECINCT": {{"values": [{n} integers or null], "total": {tot}}}}},
 "col_totals": [{n} integers or null: the small printed total under each column],
 "grand": {grand}}}
Read digits exactly as printed; do not correct or add anything up. Keep every value in the column it is printed in."""

READ_DPI = 300      # a printed digit is about 16 px tall here, against about 10 px at 200 dpi
MAX_WIDTH = 1500    # widest image sent to the model, in pixels at READ_DPI; wider ones are shrunk by the provider


def block_prompt(g, precincts):
    return BLOCK_PROMPT.format(
        n=len(precincts), precincts=", ".join(precincts),
        part="the whole" if g.labels and g.total else "a column group",
        labels=("The candidate's name is at the left (a contest title may appear above or beside it). "
                if g.labels else "The candidate's name is not in this image. "),
        total=("The last printed number at the end of each row is that row's TOTAL, and a grand total is printed "
               "under the TOTAL column at the far right. " if g.total else
               "The row TOTAL column is not in this image. "),
        contest='"the contest title if one is printed in this image, else null"' if g.labels else "null",
        candidate='"the candidate\'s name as printed, with party in brackets if shown"' if g.labels else "null",
        tot="integer" if g.total else "null", grand="the grand total under the TOTAL column" if g.total else "null")


@dataclass
class Group:
    c0: int
    c1: int          # columns c0..c1-1
    labels: bool     # includes the row-label strip at the left
    total: bool      # includes the TOTAL strip at the right
    width: float     # pixels at the read dpi


def plan_groups(edges, label_x0, total_x1, *, scale, max_w) -> list[Group]:
    """Cut the columns (n+1 edges) into runs whose image, with labels in the first and TOTAL in the last, fits max_w."""
    n = len(edges) - 1
    label_w = (edges[0] - label_x0) * scale
    total_w = (total_x1 - edges[n]) * scale
    out, c = [], 0
    while c < n:
        first = c == 0
        w = label_w if first else 0.0
        c1 = c
        while c1 < n:
            nw = w + (edges[c1 + 1] - edges[c1]) * scale
            last_extra = total_w if c1 + 1 == n else 0.0
            if c1 > c and nw + last_extra > max_w:
                break
            w, c1 = nw, c1 + 1
        last = c1 == n
        out.append(Group(c, c1, first, last, w + (total_w if last else 0.0)))
        c = c1
    return out


def merge_groups(ds: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Join group answers left to right: values and small totals concatenate; row totals and grand come from the last."""
    rows = {r: {"values": [v for d in ds for v in d["rows"][r]["values"]], "total": ds[-1]["rows"][r]["total"]}
            for r in ROWS}
    return {"contest": ds[0].get("contest"), "candidate": ds[0].get("candidate"), "rows": rows,
            "col_totals": [v for d in ds for v in d["col_totals"]], "grand": ds[-1]["grand"]}


def group_image(hi_png, b, edges, g, scale, dest: Path) -> Path:
    """Stitch the strips of one group side by side: labels | columns | TOTAL, all the block's full height."""
    y0, y1 = round(b.y0 * scale), round(b.y1 * scale)
    xs = [(b.x0, edges[0])] if g.labels else []
    xs.append((edges[g.c0], edges[g.c1]))
    if g.total:
        xs.append((edges[-1], b.x1))
    with Image.open(hi_png) as im:
        strips = [im.crop((round(a * scale), y0, round(z * scale), y1)) for a, z in xs]
    out = Image.new(strips[0].mode, (sum(s.width for s in strips), y1 - y0), 255)
    x = 0
    for s in strips:
        out.paste(s, (x, 0))
        x += s.width
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.save(dest)
    return dest


def _int_or_none(v, what):
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool)):
        return v
    raise ValueError(f"{what} must be an integer or null, got {v!r}")


def _check_list(vals, n, what):
    if not isinstance(vals, list) or len(vals) != n:
        raise ValueError(f"{what} must be a list of {n} entries, got "
                         f"{len(vals) if isinstance(vals, list) else type(vals).__name__}")
    for v in vals:
        _int_or_none(v, what)


def validator(n: int, rows=ROWS, extra=()):
    def check(d):
        if not isinstance(d, dict) or not isinstance(d.get("rows"), dict):
            raise ValueError("answer must be an object with a 'rows' object")
        for r in rows + tuple(extra):
            if r not in d["rows"]:
                raise ValueError(f"row {r} is missing")
            _check_list(d["rows"][r].get("values"), n, f"{r} values")
            _int_or_none(d["rows"][r].get("total"), f"{r} total")
        _check_list(d.get("col_totals"), n, "col_totals")
        _int_or_none(d.get("grand"), "grand")
    return check


def header_validator(d):
    p = d.get("precincts")
    if not isinstance(p, list) or not p:
        raise ValueError("precincts must be a non-empty list")
    d["precincts"] = [str(x).strip() for x in p]
    if len(set(d["precincts"])) != len(d["precincts"]):

def _edges(blocks, n):

def _box(edges, b, row_i, col_i):

    h = (b.rule_y1 - b.rule_y0) / len(ROWS)
    return (edges[col_i], round(b.rule_y0 + row_i * h), edges[col_i + 1], round(b.rule_y0 + (row_i + 1) * h))


def _store(led, county, page, bid, d, cols, contest, candidate, model, edges, b):

    for ci, col in enumerate(cols):

        led.put_total(county, page, bid, "grand", "", d["grand"])
    return stored


def _store_header(led, county, page, d, cols, model):
    n = 0
    for ci, col in enumerate(cols):
        led.put_cell(county, page, "reg", "REGISTERED", col, d["registered"]["values"][ci], contest="Registered voters",
                     model=model)
        n += 1
    if d["registered"].get("total") is not None:

    return n


def summarize(led, county):
    cells, totals = led.cells(county), led.totals(county)
    rows, cols, grand = (checks.row_checks(cells, totals), checks.column_checks(cells, totals),
                         checks.grand_checks(totals))

            "col_sums_pass": ok(cols), "col_sums_fail": len(cols) - ok(cols),
            "grand_sums_pass": ok(grand), "grand_sums_fail": len(grand) - ok(grand),
            "printed_totals": len(totals)}


def _read_block(gw, county, page, bid, b, edges, cols, png, crop_path, run_id, root, dpi):
    """One answer for the block: one call on the whole crop when the page gives no column edges, else one per group."""
    if edges is None:

def read_county(county, gw, led, *, run_id="", pages=None, dpi=200, log=print, data_root=None) -> dict:

                  crop(png, b.box, crop_path)

                                        "box": list(b.box)})
                  except BudgetExceeded:

"""Page rendering with pdftoppm, and crops with Pillow."""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

from .sources import DATA, scan_path


class RenderError(Exception):
    pass


def page_png(key: str, page: int, dpi: int = 200, root: Path = DATA) -> Path:
    """Render one page (1-based) of a county's scan to data/pages/<key>/pNN-<dpi>.png; cached."""
    out = root / "pages" / key / f"p{page:02d}-{dpi}.png"
    if out.exists():
        return out
    if shutil.which("pdftoppm") is None:
        raise RenderError("pdftoppm is not installed; install poppler-utils (apt install poppler-utils)")
    pdf = scan_path(key, root)
    if not pdf.exists():
        raise RenderError(f"{pdf} is missing; run `crossfoot fetch --county {key}` first")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    r = subprocess.run(["pdftoppm", "-png", "-r", str(dpi), "-f", str(page), "-l", str(page),
                        "-singlefile", str(pdf), str(out.with_suffix(""))],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0 or not out.exists():
        raise RenderError(f"pdftoppm failed for {pdf} page {page}: {r.stderr.strip()}")
    return out


def crop(png: Path, box: tuple[int, int, int, int], dest: Path) -> Path:
    """Crop (x0, y0, x1, y1) out of an image and save it."""
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with Image.open(png) as im:
        im.crop(box).save(dest)
    return dest
"""Finds blocks and column lines on a ruled page from the image itself. No model.

A block is a band of ink separated from the next by blank rows. A band counts as a block only if it holds a
long horizontal rule, which leaves out the footer, the signature and scanner specks. Inside a block, the column
lines are columns of dark pixels that run the height of the ruled rows; a dark run wider than a line is a
blacked-out region, reported separately.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

DARK = 110          # grey level below which a pixel is ink
MIN_GAP = 8         # blank rows that separate two blocks, in pixels at 200 dpi
RULE_FRACTION = 0.5 # share of the table width a row must cover to count as a rule
LINE_FRACTION = 0.6 # share of the ruled height a column must cover to count as a line
GRAND_DROP = 24     # pixels added below a block so the grand total is inside the crop
MAX_LINE_WIDTH = 7  # a darker run wider than this is a blackout, not a line


@dataclass
class Block:
    y0: int
    y1: int
    x0: int
    x1: int
    rule_y0: int
    rule_y1: int
    lines: list = field(default_factory=list)   # x centres of column lines
    blackouts: list = field(default_factory=list)  # (x0, x1) of dark regions wider than a line

    @property
    def box(self) -> tuple[int, int, int, int]:
        return (self.x0, self.y0, self.x1, self.y1)


def _runs(mask: np.ndarray) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Inclusive (start, end) of each run of True."""
    idx = np.flatnonzero(mask)
    if idx.size == 0:
        return []
    cuts = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(idx) > 1)
    starts = np.r_[idx[0], idx[cuts + 1]]
    ends = np.r_[idx[cuts], idx[-1]]
    return list(zip(starts.tolist(), ends.tolist()))


def find_blocks(image, *, pad: int = 6) -> list[Block]:
    im = image if isinstance(image, Image.Image) else Image.open(image)
    g = np.asarray(im.convert("L"))
    h, w = g.shape
    xl, xr = int(0.04 * w), int(0.98 * w)
    dark = g[:, xl:xr] < DARK
    # the thick bar under the TOTAL column runs down into the next block's gap, so band ink ignores the right edge
    ink = dark[:, :int(0.88 * w) - xl].sum(axis=1) >= 2
    # merge bands whose gap is below MIN_GAP
    bands: list[list[int]] = []
    for s, e in _runs(ink):
        if bands and s - bands[-1][1] <= MIN_GAP:
            bands[-1][1] = e
        else:
            bands.append([s, e])
    rule_rows = dark[:, int(0.08 * w):].mean(axis=1) >= RULE_FRACTION
    blocks = []
    for s, e in bands:
        rr = np.flatnonzero(rule_rows[s:e + 1])
        if rr.size == 0 or e - s < 20:
            continue
        r0, r1 = s + int(rr[0]), s + int(rr[-1])
        b = Block(max(0, s - pad), min(h - 1, e + pad), xl, xr, r0, r1)
        _column_lines(dark, b, xl)
        blocks.append(b)
    # the grand total hangs below the small totals at the far right, outside the band-finding range
    for b, nxt in zip(blocks, blocks[1:] + [None]):
        b.y1 = min(h - 1, b.y1 + GRAND_DROP, (nxt.y0 + 12) if nxt else h - 1)
    return blocks


def _column_lines(dark: np.ndarray, b: Block, xl: int) -> None:
    band = dark[b.rule_y0:b.rule_y1 + 1]
    if band.shape[0] < 4:
        return
    cover = band.mean(axis=0) >= LINE_FRACTION
    for s, e in _runs(cover):
        if e - s + 1 <= MAX_LINE_WIDTH:
            b.lines.append(xl + (s + e) // 2)
        else:
            b.blackouts.append((xl + s, xl + e))

"""The investigation loop's rules, with a fake model and a fake page. No network, no images of real scans."""
import json

import pytest
from PIL import Image

from crossfoot import agent, outputs, tracing
from crossfoot.ledger import Ledger

ROWS = ("EARLY", "ABSENTEE", "PRECINCT")
GOOD = {"1": (10, 2, 3), "2": (20, 4, 6)}     # column -> EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT
HAIKU, SONNET = "claude-haiku", "claude-sonnet-4.6"


def make_block(led, page, bid, good=GOOD, wrong=None, row_totals=None, col_totals=None, grand=None):
    """A block whose printed totals are those of `good`; `wrong` maps (row, column) -> the value the first read gave."""
    wrong = wrong or {}
    for col, vals in good.items():
        for r, v in zip(ROWS, vals):
            led.put_cell("x", page, bid, r, col, wrong.get((r, col), v), contest="C", candidate=f"cand {bid}")
        led.put_total("x", page, bid, "col", col, (col_totals or {}).get(col, sum(vals)))
    for i, r in enumerate(ROWS):
        led.put_total("x", page, bid, "row", r, (row_totals or {}).get(r, sum(v[i] for v in good.values())))
    led.put_total("x", page, bid, "grand", "", grand if grand is not None else sum(sum(v) for v in good.values()))


class FakeGeo:
    def __init__(self):
        self.targets = []

    def crop(self, page, bid, target, dpi, dest):
        self.targets.append((bid, dict(target), dpi))
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        Image.new("L", (10, 10), 255).save(dest)
        return dest, (0, 0, 10, 10)

    def total_box(self, page, bid, direction, key):
        return None

    def block_box(self, page, bid):
        return None


class FakeGw:
    """Decisions come from `decide(prompt, n)`, re-reads from `read(target, model, n)`. Logs every call."""
    def __init__(self, geo, decide, read, model=HAIKU):
        self.geo, self.decide, self.read, self.model = geo, decide, read, model
        self.calls = self.prompt_tokens = self.completion_tokens = 0
        self.cost = 0.0
        self.log = []

    def ask_json(self, prompt, image=None, *, validate=None, model=None):
        self.calls += 1
        model = model or self.model
        if image is None:
            ans = self.decide(prompt, sum(1 for m, k, _ in self.log if k == "decide"))
            self.log.append((model, "decide", prompt))
        else:
            bid, target, dpi = self.geo.targets[-1]
            ans = self.read(bid, target, model, sum(1 for m, k, _ in self.log if k == "read"))
            self.log.append((model, "read", (bid, target, dpi)))
        if validate:
            validate(ans)
        return ans


def reread_col(col, model=HAIKU, dpi=300):
    return {"action": "reread", "rereads": [{"target": {"kind": "column", "column": col}, "dpi": dpi, "model": model}]}


def truth_reader(good=GOOD):
    def read(bid, t, model, n):
        if t["kind"] == "column":
            e, a, p = good[t["column"]]
            return {"EARLY": e, "ABSENTEE": a, "PRECINCT": p, "total": e + a + p}
        if t["kind"] == "cell":
            return {"value": good[t["column"]][ROWS.index(t["row"])]}
        raise AssertionError(t)
    return read


def run(led, decide, read, **kw):
    geo = FakeGeo()
    gw = FakeGw(geo, decide, read)
    s = agent.close_county("x", gw, led, geo, run_id="", log=lambda *a: None, **kw)
    return s, gw, geo


def assert_status_rule(led):
    """AC-1: no accepted cell sits on a failing printed sum, and every cell ends accepted or cannot_verify."""
    from crossfoot import checks
    cells, totals = led.cells("x"), led.totals("x")
    bad = {k for ch in checks.row_checks(cells, totals) + checks.column_checks(cells, totals) if not ch.ok
           for k, _ in ch.terms}
    for c in cells:
        assert c["status"] in ("accepted", "cannot_verify"), c
        if c["status"] == "accepted":
            assert checks.cell_key(c) not in bad


def test_closes_a_misread_cell_and_records_both_readings():
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", wrong={("EARLY", "1"): 16})
    s, gw, geo = run(led, lambda p, n: reread_col("1"), truth_reader())
    assert_status_rule(led)
    assert {c["status"] for c in led.cells("x")} == {"accepted"}
    cell = next(c for c in led.cells("x") if c["row_kind"] == "EARLY" and c["column"] == "1")
    assert (cell["value"], cell["first_read"]) == (10, 16)
    ev = [e for e in led.events("x") if e["kind"] == "reread"]
    p = json.loads(ev[0]["payload_json"])
    assert p["changes"][0]["old"] == 16 and p["changes"][0]["new"] == 10 and p["model"] == HAIKU and p["dpi"] == 300
    kinds = [e["kind"] for e in led.events("x")]
    assert kinds.index("decision") < kinds.index("reread") < kinds.index("check")
    assert s["cells_changed"] == 1 and s["sums_failing_before"]["row"] == 1 and s["sums_failing_after"]["row"] == 0


def test_a_worse_reading_is_not_kept():
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", wrong={("EARLY", "1"): 16})
    # first the re-read makes it worse (EARLY 99), then it is right
    def read(bid, t, model, n):
        e, a, p = GOOD[t["column"]]
        return {"EARLY": 99 if n == 0 else e, "ABSENTEE": a, "PRECINCT": p, "total": e + a + p}
    s, gw, geo = run(led, lambda p, n: reread_col("1"), read)
    ev = [json.loads(e["payload_json"]) for e in led.events("x") if e["kind"] == "reread"]
    assert ev[0]["changes"][0]["new"] == 99 and ev[0]["changes"][0]["kept"] == "old"
    assert ev[1]["changes"][0]["kept"] == "new"
    assert_status_rule(led)


def test_row_total_misread_is_fixed_by_rereading_the_total_not_the_cells():
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", row_totals={"EARLY": 35})        # printed EARLY total misread: 35 for 30
    seen = []
    def decide(prompt, n):
        seen.append(prompt)
        return {"action": "reread", "rereads": [{"target": {"kind": "row_total", "row": "EARLY"}, "dpi": 400,
                                                 "model": HAIKU}]}
    s, gw, geo = run(led, decide, lambda b, t, m, n: {"value": 30})
    assert "look at the row's printed total first" in seen[0]
    assert [t[1]["kind"] for t in geo.targets] == ["row_total"]
    assert {c["status"] for c in led.cells("x")} == {"accepted"}
    assert all(c["value"] == c["first_read"] for c in led.cells("x"))
    assert_status_rule(led)


def test_small_total_hint_when_the_rows_pass():
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", col_totals={"1": 99})
    seen = []
    def decide(prompt, n):
        seen.append(prompt)
        return {"action": "cannot_verify", "reason": "test"}
    run(led, decide, truth_reader())
    assert "look at the small total first" in seen[0]


def test_six_actions_then_cannot_verify_and_the_loop_goes_on():
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", wrong={("EARLY", "1"): 16})
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b2", wrong={("EARLY", "2"): 21})
    stuck = lambda bid, t, m, n: ({"EARLY": 16, "ABSENTEE": 2, "PRECINCT": 3, "total": 15} if bid == "p1-b1"
                                  else {"EARLY": 20, "ABSENTEE": 4, "PRECINCT": 6, "total": 30})
    def decide(prompt, n):
        col = "1" if "p1-b1" in prompt else "2"
        return reread_col(col, model=HAIKU)
    s, gw, geo = run(led, decide, stuck)
    first = [t for t in geo.targets if t[0] == "p1-b1"]
    assert len(first) == 6
    stat = {(c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"]): c["status"] for c in led.cells("x")}
    assert stat[("p1-b1", "EARLY", "1")] == "cannot_verify"
    assert all(v == "accepted" for k, v in stat.items() if k[0] == "p1-b2")
    stops = [json.loads(e["payload_json"]) for e in led.events("x") if e["kind"] == "stop"]
    assert any("six actions" in p["reason"] for p in stops)
    assert s["cells_cannot_verify"] == 2 + 0 or s["cells_cannot_verify"] >= 1
    assert_status_rule(led)


def test_a_decision_may_list_several_rereads_and_they_count_one_each():
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", wrong={("EARLY", "1"): 16})
    many = {"action": "reread", "rereads": [{"target": {"kind": "cell", "row": "EARLY", "column": "1"},
                                             "dpi": 300, "model": HAIKU}] * 8}
    s, gw, geo = run(led, lambda p, n: many if n == 0 else {"action": "done"},
                     lambda b, t, m, n: {"value": 16})
    assert len(geo.targets) == 6


def test_stronger_model_is_refused_until_two_haiku_rereads_failed():
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", wrong={("EARLY", "1"): 16})
    plan = [reread_col("1", model=SONNET), reread_col("1"), reread_col("1"), reread_col("1", model=SONNET)]
    def read(bid, t, model, n):
        e, a, p = GOOD["1"]
        return {"EARLY": 16 if model == HAIKU else 10, "ABSENTEE": a, "PRECINCT": p, "total": e + a + p}
    s, gw, geo = run(led, lambda p, n: plan[min(n, 3)], read)
    models = [m for m, k, _ in gw.log if k == "read"]
    assert models == [HAIKU, HAIKU, SONNET]            # the first Sonnet request never reached the model
    refused = [json.loads(e["payload_json"]) for e in led.events("x") if e["kind"] == "refused"]
    assert len(refused) == 1 and "two re-reads" in refused[0]["reason"]
    assert {c["status"] for c in led.cells("x")} == {"accepted"}


def test_check_model_rule_directly():
    item = agent.Item("row", 1, "b", "EARLY")
    with pytest.raises(agent.StrongModelRefused):
        agent.check_model(item, SONNET)
    item.weak_failures = 2
    agent.check_model(item, SONNET)
    agent.check_model(item, HAIKU)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        agent.check_model(item, "some-other-model")

    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1")                                    # holds: will be accepted
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b2", wrong={("EARLY", "1"): 16})
    agent.derive_status(led, "x")
